question: On a Night 6 the phone won, driven by its own kernel touches on the game's frame clock, does any of the 65,536 seeds reproduce the night well enough to name the office seed -- and does the logged 16-candidate bracket contain it?

run.route: Night 6 binding h (artifacts/night6-cohort-h/bundle), strict anchor aim 4870 ms on 5000, maxK 0
run.outcome: WIN, 6 AM. 42 cycle gates (41 agreed, 0 corrected, 1 aborted on mask-state-unavailable at the terminal); arm VERIFIED at 9843 ms; press acceptance 3 graded (1 PASS, 2 UNKNOWN); grade-run: every instrument passed
instruments: MMFRuntime logcat streamed live (office seed bracket)
Cue Helper native frame trace, 25,565 frames, 437 s
adb getevent -lt kernel input events, 340 classified contacts
run.launcher: artifacts/forensics/seedlock-night6-20260916/run.sh (a peer Codex session started the run; this session did the analysis)

officeSeedBracket.newConfirmation: The bracket is now placed by the frame trace itself, not only by the helper's night onset: converted to the helper's monotonic clock through the campaign's paired sample (snapshotNs 928705139012432 = wallMs 1789598207421), it falls 1290.3-1305.3 ms into the trace's own 1335.1 ms office-load gap (rows 765 -> 766), ending 29.8 ms before the first frame after the gap and 59.6 ms before the first office frame (row 767). Two independent clocks agree on where the office frame was seeded.

observables.eyehole: 42 mask windows read with eyehole-read.py at video 30.284 s + game ms + 0.2 s, 3 s long: 18 occupied (4 WC, 9 WB... see string) giving ....C....BC....CB.CFB.CB..C.BC...BC..BC..B
observables.hall: 41 hall flashes read by eye at full resolution. Three luma classes: L (frame mean ~35) the beam lit, characters readable; d (~25-28) office normal but the doorway pure black, the beamless hall of g202 animation 99; D (~10-14) the whole office darkened, which is the encounter blackout sprite still fading (g535/g536 ~250 frames, cut only by a monitor raise (g845), and this route raises 140 ms AFTER the flash)
observables.crossCheck: The 17 D flashes are exactly the 17 eyehole windows before them that showed an occupant. Two independent readers of the same video agree cycle for cycle, so class D carries no information the eyehole does not; the independent parts are the d class, the standing characters (W. Bonnie at 12/17/21/30, W. Freddy at 14/35/36, the hallway Golden Freddy at 25, Mangle at 31) and Foxy's hall presence (13 present, 2 absent, 4 unreadable behind a large sprite)

harness.presses: n6-presses.py: each kernel contact (multitouch protocol B, per-slot tracking ids) is classified against the profile's controlMap through the executor's landscape transform and placed on the trace frame at touch-down + L; 338 contacts -> 505 model actions, 2 unclassified
harness.scorer: n6-score.mjs: the model under cfg.presses with frameMs from the trace's own per-frame deltas (Fusion catch-up, at most three loops per pass), every sourced draw option on, lethal. Per mask-on press it records the office encounter active in the next 1.5 s; per hall flash it records the beam state, the hall-column occupants, Foxy and the hallway Golden Freddy
harness.frameOneOrder: On night 6 the model's constructor spends one draw (the g683 one-in-ten Golden Freddy roll) before any tick, while the game spends g822 (StartOfFrame) first. The scorer builds the sim one LCG step ahead and rewinds the state so tick 1's g822 draw re-spends that step; without it every seed is scored one step out of phase
harness.latency: L = 52 ms, from this run's own monitor touch -> cameras-up static frame (269 ms - 200 ms raise - 17 ms frame)

census.setup: all 65,536 seeds at L = 52 ms, 42 eyehole windows and 41 hall flashes, 12 shards
census.totalErrors: best 29 (39435, 37732, 37937), a smooth dense distribution with no standout
census.bracketRanks: the 16 bracket seeds rank 1673-57383 of 65,536 by eyehole error (16-26 errors, mean rank 37,553): they fit the phone's night no better than random seeds
census.burnScan: for each bracket seed, walking its LCG orbit and reading the census gives the fit for any number of missing initial draws. Over 16 orbits x 2001 burns exactly one state reaches <= 6 errors (51376 + 1589 draws), against 0.98 expected by chance: no small stream offset rescues the bracket

discriminatingPower.selfRecovery: Using each of 400 model nights as the target, the true seed scores 0 and the best wrong seed scores 4-13 (mean 8.7, sd 1.4). So the observable can separate a true seed from 65,535 wrong ones -- when the target really is a model night
discriminatingPower.phoneAgainstThat: The phone's best (5) is reached by a wrong seed in 1.0% of model nights (4/400), and <= 6 in 4.8%. Suggestive, not a lock
discriminatingPower.informationContent: the 42 windows carry 59.7 bits against the 16 needed; matching the phone window by window narrows 65,536 seeds to 6 by window 16, 1 by window 18 (seed 59936) and 0 by window 19 -- the funnel a chance cascade produces, since 59936's whole-night error is 16

latencyRobustness.setup: 1,539 probe seeds (the L=52 top 40, the 16 bracket seeds, 1,500 random) rescored at L = 40, 46, 58 and 64 ms
latencyRobustness.result: seed 39435 goes from 5 errors at L=52 to 18 at all four other latencies. Each latency has a different best seed (32027, 32889, 39435, 14304, 51386) at 5-12 errors; the whole L=52 top 40 degrades to 15-24. The fit landscape is reshuffled by a 6 ms change in the assumed latency, so any best seed at a fixed L is an artefact of that L
latencyRobustness.decorrelation: for the same seed, a 6 ms change in L changes the night from eyehole window 11-16 (median; p10 = 7) and a 12 ms change from window 11-13; 0 of 1,539 nights are identical at any of the four offsets

verdict: SEED PICKED BY TIMING THE FIRST FRAME. The bytecode places the seeding call between two adjacent log lines, which pins this night to 51376 or 51377 and pins two earlier k3 nights to a single seed each (full-06 47593, full-04 34043). The model-based census and the 51380 pick are superseded: the model is not faithful enough to name a seed, and it does not have to be, because the clock does it. NO LOCK, and the blocker is now measured rather than assumed. The observable has enough information (59.7 bits, 16 needed) and enough separating power (wrong seeds floor at 6-13 errors against a known model night). What defeats it is that the model's trajectory decorrelates under the input-latency uncertainty at the same point the information arrives: 16 bits have accumulated only by window ~16, while a 6 ms latency error already changes the night by window ~11. The seed bracket is not the problem -- it is confirmed by a second clock, and no bracket seed fits at any stream offset up to 2000 draws.
consequence: A seed lock needs the information delivered inside the first 6-8 cycles, before the latency uncertainty decorrelates the trajectory. The current route gives 4.4 bits in windows 0-7 and 1.3 bits per cycle at steady state.

The cheapest way to get there is more observations per cycle, not more cycles: a route whose monitor time steps through several cameras would read a position vector per raise instead of one office cue, and the video already resolves those feeds.
Failing that, the per-touch registration loop must be pinned to about one frame, which is the same blocker the k3 touch-trace night recorded on 2026-09-16.

modelFix.change: g822 (Paper Pals AI = (Random(100)+1)/100) is an application StartOfFrame event, not Always: its condition is (objectType -3, num -1), and only num -1 on objectType -1 is the system Always. The model drew it once per frame, about 60 spurious draws per second
modelFix.checked: regenerated the CCN dump from ~/fnaf-tools/ctfak-src and read the group directly; mmfparser's condition name table (chunkloaders/conditions/names.py) gives -3/-1 = StartOfFrame and -1/-1 = Always; the Chowdren recompile puts the same draw in on_frame_4_start_events
modelFix.now: one draw before the first loop, ahead of g811's first viewing = 0 draw; g58/g192 every 6 frames and g59 at 29/30 are unchanged
modelFix.credit: found and written by a peer Codex session in the same worktree; verified here against the dump before committing

nextRoute.question: How much sooner would a route that surveys cameras during its monitor time name the seed?
nextRoute.method: n6-positions.mjs records every unit's node, Foxy's and the Puppet's at each monitor raise. Censused over all 65,536 seeds on this run's own presses (first 8,000 frames), the survey signature is, per raise, the sorted unit set standing on each surveyed camera.

result.6 cams {8,7,4,3,10,9}: 12.08 bits / 17% of seeds uniquely named by raise 5, 15.08 / 65% by raise 7, 15.65 / 83% by raise 8 (75 s), 15.96 / 97% by raise 10
result.this run's eyehole route: 2.02 bits / 0% by window 5, 4.18 / 0% by window 7, 7.51 / 1% by window 10, 14.81 / 49% by window 18

nextRoute.decorrelation: the survey signature is no more stable than the eyehole under latency error (first differing raise at 6 ms: median 9-14, p10 5-6), so the gain is entirely in speed: a six-camera survey delivers 16 bits at raise 7-8, before the median decorrelation point, where the eyehole route needs window 18, well after it.
nextRoute.caveat: on night 6 the three Toys sit at CAM 9 until 2 AM, so the early bits come from the three Withereds and Mangle; a night whose dials are all live from the first hour would separate faster.
nextRoute.proposal: a Night 6 seed-lock route identical to binding h except that the monitor-up stretch steps through the six already-calibrated cameras {4,7,8,9,10,11} instead of parking on CAM 11, reading each feed from the video. Lock decided on raises 0-8 (the first 75 s), with the rest of the night unchanged so the 6 AM result is still a graded run.
nextRoute.calibratedSet: The profile already carries tap points for cams 4, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 and for no others, so no new geometry is needed -- and that set is better than the {8,7,4,3,10,9} guessed above: 13.42 bits / 26% of seeds uniquely named by raise 5, 15.54 / 76% by raise 7, 15.84 / 90% by raise 8 (75 s), 15.99 / 98% by raise 10. Adding cam 3 would need a calibrated tap and buys only 82% vs 76% at raise 7. Build the route on {4,7,8,9,10,11}.

pick.question: Constrained to the 16 seeds the game log brackets, is exactly one consistent with the phone's night?
pick.method: Score the observations in time order -- mask window k, then hall flash k -- and stop at the first mismatch, so a wrong seed cannot be rescued by lucky late agreement. The dim hall class is skipped because the model reproduces it only 12% of the time. Scanned over L = 20..100 ms in 2 ms steps.
pick.firstEncounterFilter: The hall reads bound the first encounter independently of the eyehole: flash 3 (44.9 s) is lit with no blackout, and window 4 (49.2 s) shows Withered Chica, so the first encounter began between 44.9 and 50.5 s and it was Withered Chica. Of the 16 x 41 (seed, latency) pairs, only 34 reproduce that -- seeds 51380 and 51381, and only at L >= 68 ms. This contradicts the L = 52 ms taken from this run's monitor-touch-to-static measurement, and agrees with the k3 night, whose best fit was 83 ms.
pick.result: 51381 fails at observation 3 (it puts Withered Bonnie in the hall where the phone shows only Foxy). Seed 51380 tracks the phone for 16 consecutive observations, through window 8 and flash 8 (about 85 s), then misses the phone's Withered Bonnie at window 9. Every other bracket seed stops at 8 or earlier, at every latency from 68 to 100 ms -- the separation is a broad plateau, not a spike at one latency.
pick.statistics: At a fixed L = 84 ms over all 65,536 seeds, 325 (0.496%) reach an unbroken prefix of 16 or more; the global best is 26 (seed 62826, outside the bracket). So a wrong bracket seed clears 16 with probability 0.005, and the chance that any of the 15 wrong ones would is 7%. Within the bracket the posterior odds for 51380 are about 13:1 under the neutral assumption that the model is as likely to carry a true seed to 16 as to break it by 8, and higher if it tracks a true seed better than that.
pick.verdict: PICK, not a lock: seed 51380 at L = 84-94 ms, at roughly 13:1 within the bracket. This is the first single-seed pick from a clock bracket on any night here. It rests on the bracket being right, which two independent clocks now support, and on the model being faithful over the first 85 s. It is not a lock, because the global best fit over all 65,536 seeds (26 observations) lies outside the bracket, which means the model is still unfaithful enough for chance to beat the truth over a whole night.
modelDefectsIsolated: The model's encounter timing slips whole 10 s cycles against the phone. For 51380 at L=84 the office cues are 48.8, 118.8, 148.8, 158.8, 188.8, 198.8, 218.8, 228.8 s while the phone's are 49.2, 99.2, 109.2, 159.2, 169.2, 189.2, 199.2, 209.2, 229.2, 239.2: the pair structure is right and three pairs line up exactly, but others sit one cycle out. That slip, not the seed, is what ends the prefix.

At L >= 68 ms the model kills through Foxy's g573 at 225-265 s on a night the phone won, for every seed tried. Suppressing that kill (it has no RNG side effects) does not change any prefix, so it is a separate defect, but it means model survival cannot be used as an observable at the latency the first encounter requires.
pick.next: Fix the cycle slip in the encounter timing and rescore: if 51380 then tracks well past 85 s while the other fifteen stay at 8, the pick becomes a lock. Independently, a second night with the pick predeclared -- predict the first encounter's character and time from the clock bracket alone, then read the video -- would confirm it without any further model work.

firstFrameTiming.question: Can the office frame's seed be pinned by timing the first frame, instead of searching seeds against the model?
firstFrameTiming.bytecode: classes.dex, read with dexread3.py. CRunApp.startTheFrame logs "Starting new frame" at instruction 42, calls MMFRuntime.updateViewport at 113 (whose block ends with "Setting renderer limits..."), then centerDisplay, CreateLayerEffects, flushKeyboard and new CRun, and only calls CRun.initRunLoop at 231. allocRunHeader -- the one currentTimeMillis that becomes rh3Graine -- is instruction 0 of initRunLoop, ahead of initAsmLoop (16), y_InitLevel (19), prepareFrame (22), createFrameObjects (29, whose object creation reaches CExtLoad.loadRunObject and logs "Created extension: ") and f_InitLoop (57, which logs "iPhoneOptions are "). initRunLoop then takes a second currentTimeMillis at 64 into rhTimerOld, the loop clock's origin.
firstFrameTiming.rule: The seed is taken strictly between the last line logged before initRunLoop and the first line logged inside it. The old bracket -- "Starting new frame" to the next "startTheFrame() called" -- spans the whole of createFrameObjects and is 13 to 16 ms wide; the sourced one is one or two.
firstFrameTiming.retraction: This refutes the model-based pick of 51380 recorded above: 51380 is 1789598222516, four milliseconds past the first "Created extension" line, so the runtime had already seeded and moved on. The pick was a 7% false positive and is withdrawn. The clock, not the model, names the seed.
firstFrameTiming.consequenceForTheModel: For the clock's candidates the model puts the night's first office encounter at 78.8 s (Withered Chica, at L = 84-92 ms) where the phone had it at about 49 s: the right character, three cycles late. That is now a sharply localised defect to fix -- a named seed, a named moment, a named error -- rather than a diffuse divergence.
firstFrameTiming.tooling: tools/device/office-seed-bracket.py applies the sourced rule by default and keeps the old one behind --legacy-pair; it names which rule it used in its JSON. test-office-seed-bracket.py covers both and the fallback for a log with nothing from inside initRunLoop, and runs in npm run test:contracts.

modelGapMeasuredOnAWinningNight.artifact: night6-c2-01-20260917T021417Z: 6 AM, all 42 cycle gates AGREED, office seed named to a single millisecond (low16 24851). No frame trace was kept, but none is needed to drive the model: the plan is deterministic, every gate agreed, and the executor's release instant (1789611309534) and the seed instant (1789611303187) are the same phone wall clock, so the presses sit 6347 ms after the model's frame 1.
modelGapMeasuredOnAWinningNight.result: At its own seed the model dies at 150.2 s to Golden Freddy. Censused over 600 seeds on the same presses it dies in ALL 600: 368 Foxy, 220 Golden Freddy, 12 inside-office. With Golden Freddy disabled it still dies in all 600: 551 Foxy, 46 inside-office, 3 Puppet. The phone reached 6 AM.
modelGapMeasuredOnAWinningNight.reading: This is the model gap stated as a measurement rather than a suspicion, and it is not a seeding artefact: no seed survives. The route flashes the hall once per cycle, and both dominant causes are hall-flash kill rules -- Foxy's g573 and Golden Freddy's g778. Foxy alone accounts for 551 of 600. Whatever keeps the phone's Foxy from killing through 42 flashes is not in the model.
modelGapMeasuredOnAWinningNight.goldenFreddyLead: g336, which creates Golden Freddy, carries five conditions: the 5 s timer, Random(20) < GF AI, viewing > 0, no yellowbear yet, and `mmonitorUp.Active` INVISIBLE (condition -28 is ObjectInvisible in mmfparser's table). The model approximates the last two with `monitor === MON_UP`. If that sprite is visible while the monitor is up, the source creates him far more rarely than the model does, which would explain 220 deaths in 600 that the phone never suffers. Resolving that sprite's visibility lifecycle is the next source question.
modelGapMeasuredOnAWinningNight.next: Fix Foxy first: it is 92% of the deaths with Golden Freddy removed. The census harness is artifacts/forensics/twin-nights-night6-cohort2/ plus the scratch scorer that runs without a frame trace; re-run it after any change and the pass mark is simple -- some seed must survive a route the phone survived.
modelGapMeasuredOnAWinningNight.notTheSourcedChain: Re-censused with the sourced Foxy chain replaced by the legacy one (sourcedFoxyChain and sourcedDropLightOrder off, Golden Freddy off, unhooked so the model accepts it): 594 of 600 still die to Foxy, 6 inside-office, none survive. So the defect is not the 2026-09-15 chain rewrite; both implementations share the premise that a hall flash with Foxy at the got-you box ends the night, and on this route the phone took 42 flashes and reached 6 AM.
modelGapMeasuredOnAWinningNight.latchIsSourced: The flash is not instantaneous in the source and the model has this right: g488 zeroes `viewing hall light` on a 1000 ms timer and g489 sets it to 1 on any frame with viewing == 0, battery > 0 and `lit?` == 1, so a 33 ms flash leaves the counter latched for up to a second. g573 then needs Foxy at marker 123 with viewing 0, that latch, no committed attack and no blackout, and it sets `being attacked by` = 4 rather than killing directly -- but g267/g270 refuse the mask once that is non-zero, so it is a kill in effect.
modelGapMeasuredOnAWinningNight.whereToLookNext: Since both chains kill, the wrong premise is upstream of the kill: either Foxy reaches marker 123 far more often in the model than in the game, or something on this route keeps the phone's Foxy off it. The route flashes the camera light every cycle with the monitor up and does a camdrop that holds the light through the drop, so g864's CAM 08 drain and g846's retreat are both live on the phone; those are the rules to check against a night whose hall reads show Foxy standing in the hall for most of it without ever killing.
